tier2: rating >= 4 and no build red flag (weak-archetype flag excluded, see archetype_flag)

review.verdict: Strong RG deck with bombs like Screaming Nemesis and Tyvar plus plenty of removal (Chainsaw, Dragonfire, 3 Glassworks, Clobbering) and solid delirium enablers. The very low curve and modest creature count leave it a little thin on board presence, but it's a well-built aggressive deck.

decks.playmat_name: ★★ good_01 · RG+b aggro-removal (light B splash) · review 4/5

review.verdict: A strong RG deck with premium removal (3 Dragonfire, 2 Glassworks, Overlord) and solid threats like Enduring Courage and Fear of Missing Out; the black splash for only Swarmweaver is marginal and a few slots like Glimmerlight and Fungus are filler, but the deck is well built.

Solid removal suite (Dragonfire, Bargain, Inferno, Beastie Beatdown) and good haste top end (Wurm, Hordecaller, Rootwise) carry a deck padded with low-impact filler like 2x Glimmerlight, Saw, Frantic Strength and Percussionists, and its 11 real creatures are thin for an aggro plan.

Plenty of cheap red removal (2 Dragonfire, Chainsaw, Bargain, Inferno, 2 Beatdown) and a low curve suited to 16 lands. But only 12 real creatures, mostly small ones like Percussionist, Playmate and Hand That Feeds, plus inconsistent delirium enablers, leave it light on pressure and board presence.

Strong red removal (2 Dragonfire, 2 Glassworks, Beatdown) and solid tops in Hordecaller and Fear of Being Hunted, but thin on real creatures and padded with weak cards like Percussionist, Violent Urge and Patchwork Beastie with few delirium enablers; a fine but unexceptional deck.

A solid RG shell with Overlord of the Hauntwoods, Valgavoth's Onslaught, Kona and four fight/burn removal spells. But it has only 12 real creatures and leans on three Manifest Dread plus weak filler like Glimmerlight and Turn Inside Out, so it's a fine deck rather than a strong one.

A real RG delirium shell with good red removal (Bargain x2, Dragonfire, Emergence, Beatdown), but it leans on three Patchwork Beasties and three Say Its Name without Altanak, so creature quality is thin and the deck depends on hitting delirium; the curve is heavy at two with almost nothing at 3–5.

Solid removal (Dragonfire, Beatdown, Emergence, Waltz) and strong payoffs in Hordecaller, Onslaught and three Slayers, but only 12 real creatures, and weak filler like Norin, Vengeful Possession with no sac outlet, Turn Inside Out and Glimmerlight make it a fine but unspectacular aggro deck.

A solid RG aggro shell with good burn (2 Dragonfire, Inferno, Emergence), Fear of Being Hunted, Hordecaller and Onslaught. It is held back by only 13 true creatures, durdly slots like Ghost Vacuum, Norin and Charred Foyer, and a thin top end.

Solid RG beats with strong tops in 2x Fear of Burning Alive, Enduring Courage, Chainsaw and Wickerfolk. Interaction is thin, and cards like Norin, Violent Urge, Patchwork Beastie and a lone Say Its Name lower the quality.

A low-curve RG delirium deck with strong removal (2 Glassworks, Chainsaw, Bargain, Emergence) and good card-type diversity. Two Fungus, two Turn Inside Out and the delirium-gated Beasties are weak filler, and there are only 14 real creatures with little top end. Fine, not special.

Four Beastie Beatdowns plus Glassworks, Bargain and Fear of Burning Alive give it plenty of removal, but the small 1-2 drop bodies (Percussionists, Norin, Playmates) are weak fight partners and the 12-creature count leans heavily on manifest dread to keep the Beatdowns live.

Strong top end and removal (Nemesis, Enduring Courage, Fear of Burning Alive, Inferno, Dragonfire, Waltz) carry a deck light on real creatures, with filler 2-drops like Say Its Name diluting the aggressive curve.

Solid RG midrange with strong removal (Dragonfire, Inferno, Waltz, Beatdown, Emergence) and good threats like Hordecaller, Enduring Courage and Branchsnapper. Patchwork Beastie, Hand That Feeds, Turn Inside Out and Vengeful Possession are weak filler, and delirium will be hard to turn on reliably.

A low, fast RG aggro deck: 4 Wildfire Wickerfolk, 4 Wary Watchdog and a good removal suite (Chainsaw, Trial of Agony, Beastie Beatdown, Inferno, 2 Emergence) make it solid, but with almost nothing above 3 mana it can run out of gas, and its delirium enablers are thin for Patchwork Beastie.

Plenty of quality removal (Dragonfire x2, Inferno, Bargain), and the Say Its Name package makes Altanak a real late-game plan. But only 9 true creatures and three cantrip-style Say Its Names leave the deck thin on threats, which also hurts Beatdown and Monstrous Emergence.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_16 · RG+b delirium aggro (light B splash) · review 3/5

review.verdict: A solid RG delirium shell: Chainsaw, Beastie Beatdown, Tyvar, Balustrade Wurm and two Fear of Burning Alive give it real power, and the artifact, enchantment and creature card types help delirium. But removal is thin. Cathartic Parting, Violent Urge and Vengeful Possession are weak slots, and splashing two gold black cards for modest payoff is questionable.

A low-curve RG beatdown deck with good red removal (3 Scorching Dragonfire, Chainsaw, Betrayer's Bargain) and strong pieces in Hordecaller and Fear of Exposure; it is held back by weak one-drops (Percussionists, Turn Inside Out, Violent Urge) and unreliable delirium for Patchwork Beastie, making it a fine but unspectacular deck.

Solid removal (2 Dragonfire, 2 Glassworks, Bargain) and good green threats like Enduring Vitality, Fear of Exposure and Thresher. But the low curve leans on weak 1–2 drops (Percussionist, Playmate, Fungus), Say Its Name is filler, and delirium payoffs are underfed, so it plays as a fine but unspectacular deck.

A solid red-heavy RG deck with real removal (Bargain, Glassworks, 2 Inferno) and decent threats, but the two Islands only serve the back half of one Room. They should be Mountains to fix a mana base that is short on red sources, and several filler cards (Beastie, Playmate, Turn Inside Out) keep it average.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_20 · RG+b delirium midrange (B splash) · review 3/5

review.verdict: A strong red removal suite (3 Glassworks, 3 Impossible Inferno, Fear of Burning Alive) carries a thin 12-creature deck, and the black splash spends fixing on mediocre cards like Fanatic of the Harrowing and Broodspinner rather than bombs.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_21 · RG+b delirium midrange (light B splash) · review 3/5

review.verdict: Strong red-green removal suite (Beastie Beatdown x2, Betrayer's Bargain x2, Glassworks, Fear of Burning Alive) with decent delirium enablers. But only about 11 real creatures strains the fight and bite effects, the black splash buys just one Swarmweaver, and Peer Past the Veil and Say Its Name are filler, so it's a solid but unspectacular deck.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_22 · RG+b delirium (light B splash) · review 3/5

review.verdict: A coherent, low-curve RG delirium deck with plenty of card-type enablers, Overlord of the Hauntwoods as a strong top end and a cheap Swarmweaver splash, but Turn Inside Out, two Found Footage and only three real removal spells keep it around average.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_23 · RG+b delirium aggro (light B splash) · review 3/5

review.verdict: Solid RG delirium shell with good removal (3 Beastie Beatdown, Dragonfire, Inferno) and decent threats like Hordecaller and Wickerfolk, but only 13 real creatures for creature-dependent fight spells, and splashing two gold Broodspinners on 3 black sources is clunky; cutting them for on-color bodies would tighten it.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_24 · RG+w delirium midrange splash W · review 3/5

review.verdict: Strong red removal suite (Dragonfire, Bargain, 2x Glassworks, Emergence) plus manifest dread value carries a light creature count. Overlord is a strong splash, Toby is a weaker one, and Ghost Vacuum is filler.

decks.playmat_name: ★ good_25 · RG+b G-based delirium, R/B split · review 3/5

review.verdict: Solid green delirium core with good removal (2 Dragonfire, Glassworks, Drag to the Roots) and plenty of graveyard enablers, but it is really three colors: two BG Broodspinners and an RG Wickerfolk run on only 4-5 off-color sources, and the creature count is thin.
